newsitem.title: USA: Wackenhut to guard U.S. Embassy in Rome.
newsitem.headline: Wackenhut to guard U.S. Embassy in Rome.

text.p: Security services provider Wackenhut Corp said on Friday its Italian joint-venture received a U.S. Department of State contract to provide security services to the U.S. Embassy in Rome.
The company said in a statement the contract started in October 1996 and would generate revenues of about $5 million over the next five years.
President and Chief Operating Officer Richard Wackenhut said the contract was an important part of its European expansion plans.
The embassy had been guarded by United Mondialpol International, which was owned by U.S.-based United International Investigative Services, Wackenhut said.
A Wackenhut spokesman said the company had been fighting for over a year to win the contract.
Since United Mondialpol was a registered Italian company, it was not entitled to certain preferences from the U.S. embassy, the Wackenhut spokesman said.
